official_sources: Strategic environmental assessment and sustainability appraisal
Making local plan documents publicly available
Environmental Assessment of Plans and Programmes Regulations 2004
Town and Country Planning Local Planning England Regulations 2026
official_measurement_examples: sustainability appraisal is a plan-making process not a project permission
SEA environmental assessment is distinct from project EIA
SA generally incorporates SEA requirements for local plans
reasonable alternatives must be assessed in plan context
neighbourhood plans do not have a general statutory SA duty but SEA can still be required
SPD may exceptionally require SEA where significant effects are likely
2026 local-plan transition does not convert plan assessment into parcel permission
SEA/SA evidence does not establish parcel ownership or development yield
core_rules: SEA/SA is plan-level not parcel clearance
reasonable alternatives are plan evidence not parcel options
screening determination is not plan adoption
environmental report is not plan adoption
neighbourhood SA and SEA duties must remain distinct
2026 plan-system transition does not erase assessment duties
plan assessment does not establish ownership
plan assessment does not prove infrastructure capacity
plan assessment does not calculate development yield
no parcel SEA clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: GOV.UK, Planning Inspectorate and legislation sources checked 2026-07-26. Current 2026 local-plan system context retained with SEA/SA/EIA/HRA distinctions; no parcel promotion.
